planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained, evenly moist soil in partial shade to filtered sun; Compacta is one of the slowest-growing boxwoods available and suits rock gardens, edging, and miniature or bonsai use where its tiny stature can be appreciated up close.

directions: Plant in well-drained, evenly moist soil in partial shade to filtered sun, siting it where its extremely slow growth and tiny stature can be appreciated up close rather than lost among larger shrubs. Compacta is among the slowest-growing boxwoods in cultivation, often adding only a few inches over many years, which has made it a long-standing favorite for rock gardens, miniature and railroad-garden scenes, and bonsai training. Its dense, tight branching resists winter bronzing better when given some afternoon shade in colder zones, and established plants need only light shearing every year or two to keep their naturally neat mounded form. Avoid soggy sites, since good drainage is essential to prevent root rot in this fine-rooted dwarf selection.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Newport Blue holds a cool blue-green foliage tone through winter that sets it apart from green-leaved boxwood cultivars in mixed plantings.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade, allowing room for its slow but steady growth into a dense, rounded mound. Newport Blue is valued for cool blue-green foliage that holds its color through winter better than many green-leaved boxwoods, giving it a distinct look in mixed borders and foundation plantings. Its tight, naturally tidy habit needs only minimal shearing to maintain a clean form, and established plants tolerate summer heat and light shade with little dieback. Protect from harsh, drying winter wind in the coldest part of its range to prevent foliage bronzing.

common_name: Golden Dream Boxwood (Peergold Gold-Margined Littleleaf Boxwood)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in fertile, well-drained, consistently moist soil in partial shade to full sun; Golden Dream keeps its gold-edged variegation best with some protection from the most intense afternoon sun.

directions: Plant in fertile, well-drained, consistently moist soil in partial shade to full sun, where its gold-edged foliage brightens without scorching in intense afternoon heat. Introduced under the trade name Golden Dream from the cultivar Peergold, this compact, slow-growing boxwood has green leaves rimmed in clear yellow, giving it a variegated presence distinct from the solid-green boxwoods that dominate most collections. It shows good resistance to boxwood leafminer and tolerates boxwood blight pressure better than many older cultivars, making it a lower-maintenance option for hedging and edging. Light shearing in late spring after new growth hardens keeps the mounded form dense and the variegation showing throughout the plant.

common_name: Umpqua Chief Nandina (Tall Old-Line Heavenly Bamboo)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Umpqua Chief is a tall, old-line nandina selection best used for screening and background plantings rather than small foundation beds.

directions: Plant in well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade, spacing plants to allow the upright canes room to form a dense screen or background planting. Umpqua Chief is one of the taller, old-line nandina selections bred in Oregon, valued for foliage that turns a deep purplish red in winter cold and for heavy clusters of orange-red berries that persist into the colder months. Its larger scale and vigorous cane growth suit it to hedges and property-line screening rather than small foundation beds where compact modern cultivars are more appropriate. Thin out the oldest canes at ground level every few years to renew vigor and keep the planting from becoming top-heavy.

common_name: Umpqua Warrior Nandina (Tall Fast-Growing Fine-Textured Heavenly Bamboo)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained soil in full sun; Umpqua Warrior grows faster and taller than most nandina cultivars and is best suited to screening and tall hedges rather than compact plantings.

directions: Plant in well-drained soil in full sun for the deepest winter foliage color, giving this fast-growing, upright nandina room to reach its full mature height as a screen or hedge. Umpqua Warrior grows faster and taller than most nandina selections, with finer-textured leaflets that turn a fiery, dark red through winter and abundant red berry clusters that persist for months. Because of its vigorous, cane-forming habit it is best used for screening, tall hedges, or background plantings rather than foundation use. Renewal-prune by removing the oldest canes at the base periodically to maintain density and prevent a leggy, top-heavy silhouette.

common_name: Petite Jade Aucuba (Compact Blight-Resistant Japanese Laurel)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in evenly moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Petite Jade shows notably better resistance to anthracnose-type leaf blight than many older aucuba selections.

directions: Plant in evenly moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, where its glossy foliage resists the leaf scorch that troubles aucuba in sunnier sites. Selected from material collected at Chollipo Arboretum in South Korea, Petite Jade forms a dense, rounded mound and shows notably better resistance to the anthracnose-type leaf blight that disfigures many older aucuba plantings. Its solid deep-green leaves and compact, well-branched habit make it a reliable filler for shaded foundation beds, woodland gardens, and shady courtyards where variegated aucuba cultivars can look busy. Established plants tolerate heavy shade and dry spells better than sun exposure, so keep it out of direct afternoon sun in warm climates.

common_name: Sizzling Pink Loropetalum (Reblooming Burgundy Fringe Flower)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in humus-rich, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun to partial shade; Sizzling Pink flowers heaviest in spring with scattered rebloom through the growing season.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun to partial shade, giving Sizzling Pink room to develop its rounded, bushy form. This selection holds deep burgundy new growth that matures to an olive-purple green, and it produces spidery, ribbon-petaled pink flowers in a heavy spring flush with scattered rebloom through the rest of the growing season. Full sun brings out the richest foliage color and heaviest bloom, while some afternoon shade in the hottest climates helps prevent leaf scorch. Prune immediately after the spring bloom period if size control is needed, since shearing later in the season removes the wood that would otherwise flower next year.
